text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 billing persists after risk adjustment, with the excess concentrated in sicker patients, but the documentation is too thin to say whether it reflects upcoding or a genuinely complex panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The 99215 share is above the all-provider rate in every complexity band, including 1-2 condition patients. Most 99215s fall on patients with 5+ conditions, where the sampled claims (e.g., C0183572, C0183677) show multimorbid patients consistent with high-complexity visits. The low-complexity 99215s are a small share but worth a look, since sampled claims such as C0183233 and C0183688 (same patient, diabetes only) and C0183580 (hypertension only) carry little diagnosis support for the highest level. The four documented 99215s all supported high MDM, and only one moderate-plus data note lacked a lab line, but with records for just 16 claims this neither clears nor implicates the provider. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215s and a larger sample of 99214/99215 claims in the 1-3 condition bands, where the gap from peers is widest relative to patient need."}
